title: Kth Smallest Element in a BST
contract: For a valid strict BST and 1 ≤ k ≤ node count, return the kth smallest value.
brute: List<Integer> all=new ArrayList<>();collect(tree(input),all);Collections.sort(all);emit("Collect and sort all values","values",all);return all.get(k-1);
optimal: Tree node=tree(input);Deque<Tree> stack=new ArrayDeque<>();while(node!=null||!stack.isEmpty()){while(node!=null){stack.push(node);node=node.left;}node=stack.pop();emit("Inorder visits the next smallest value","value",node.value,"remaining rank",k);if(--k==0)return node.value;node=node.right;}throw new IllegalArgumentException("Invalid rank");
reasoning: Sorting collected values ignores the ordering already encoded by the BST.
Inorder traversal yields increasing values; stop when k nodes have been popped.
This saves work for a small k. Repeated rank queries under updates may justify storing subtree sizes in a balanced order-statistic tree.
